newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Red-hot Taiwan stocks close at another 6-yr high.
newsitem.headline: Red-hot Taiwan stocks close at another 6-yr high.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply higher on Monday, shattering the previous six-year peak set on Saturday as investors remained confident in the market's upside potential, brokers said.

The weighted index, which rose throughout most of the session, ended 88.25 points, or 1.16 percent, higher at 7,687.18. That surpassed the 7,598.93 finish on Saturday and was the market's highest close since ending at 7,857.01 on June 2, 1990.
Turnover was a hectic T$130.56 billion.
The market has finished higher in 10 of the last 11 sessions and gained more than 500 points over that span.

"The market doesn't seem to be showing any signs of letting up despite having risen so much already," said Oliver Fang, senior analyst for National Securities. "The large turnover means it is a liquidity-driven rally."
Electronics shares, buoyed by recent gains in the sector on major foreign markets including Wall Street, rose 1.54 percent, with computer motherboard giant Asustek gaining T$13 to close at T$421.
Asset-backed, property and construction shares all benefited from widespread hope that Taiwan's economy would see a recovery in 1997.
